scaffold.title: THE WORLD OF BLEACH
scaffold.lede: Every soul leaves a shadow. Every blade has a name.
scaffold.note: The hero, the five layers and fifteen sections are in place. The remaining sections arrive in turn.

world.playgroundNote: This route carries no content: it exercises the five world palettes, the depth rail and the Senkaimon transition together. The sections arrive in a separate pass.

hero.title: BLEACH
hero.subtitle: THE CYCLE OF SOULS
hero.lede: The balance between life and death rests on a war no one has seen for a thousand years.

gotei.title: Gotei 13
gotei.lede: Thirteen divisions, thirteen gates. Faithful to Seireitei's circular plan: Sōkyoku Hill at the centre, the gates of a soul army around it. In canon every division has a flower, and every flower a meaning.

zanpakuto.title: Zanpakutō Archives
zanpakuto.lede: A Zanpakutō is not a weapon but a living soul. So this is not a list of techniques but a catalogue of living things: every blade has a line of transformation, and six of them have an inner world. The release commands were verified against canon.

bankai.title: Bankai Hall
bankai.lede: A dark corridor. Closed silhouettes stand in the wall niches and none of them is named — a Bankai is a secret. The name appears only when light falls on it. Walk to the right.

hierarchy.title: The Soul Hierarchy
hierarchy.lede: In the spirit world power is not spread out, it is stacked. At the top sits a seal no one may touch; at the bottom, the eightieth district. Every floor in between answers to the one above it — go down.
hierarchy.descentAria: The soul hierarchy, top to bottom

hollow.title: The Breaking of the Mask
hollow.lede: Hollow evolution is not a family tree: it is what happens to a single mask. It is put on, it swells, it narrows, it cracks, and in the end it breaks — and what comes out from under it is a human face. Seven stages, each of them guarded by a prohibition.
hollow.stagesAria: The seven stages of Hollow evolution

espada.title: The Ten Who Answer
espada.lede: The ten strongest Arrancar in Aizen's army. But this is not a power list: in Baraggan's words, each of them holds dominion over a different form of death. That is why the centre here is a number and not a portrait — the roster is not a gallery but a typology.
espada.courtAria: The Espada, in order of strength
espada.ceroUnknown: not recorded in canon — the default cero is crimson
espada.sceneLine: If I could have held it in my hand, if I could have seen it…

wandenreich.title: The Invisible Empire
wandenreich.lede: Everything up to here has been Japanese; this is European gothic, and the collision is deliberate. The Quincy are an empire too: one name at the top, a guard of five beneath it, and at the bottom an alphabet of twenty-six letters. The emperor hands the letters out.
wandenreich.schriftNote: a single-letter power engraved into a Quincy's body
wandenreich.hint: Point at a letter, or press A–Z on the keyboard
wandenreich.gridAria: The Sternritter alphabet, A to Z

powers.title: The Spiritual Power System
powers.lede: Three races, three systems of power and three separate design languages. These powers do not resemble one another, so here they are not made to look alike: ink, void and geometry stand side by side without touching.
powers.zankensoki: the four basic arts, under one name
powers.blutRule: Offence and defence run through two separate reishi systems and, as Urahara puts it, both cannot be active at once. The choice above works the same way: switch one on and the other goes out by itself.

masks.title: The Wall of Masks
masks.lede: Say Bleach and a mask is what comes to mind. Eight of them hang from a single line: seven have an owner, the eighth does not. It is that last one which keeps this wall from being a display case.

war.title: The Thousand-Year Blood War
war.lede: The bill for a blow left unfinished a thousand years ago. Across this section the page turns from black to blood in four stops: ink, bone white, dark blood and blood. As you descend, the line on the left comes apart too.
war.timelineAria: The Thousand-Year Blood War, nine events

legends.title: The Legends
legends.lede: Ten names, ten weights holding up three worlds. There is no ranking between them — which is why there are no numbers here. Point at a name: the whole section turns to their reiatsu.
legends.hint: Point at a name, or choose one with the keyboard

houses.title: The Noble Houses
houses.lede: In Bleach the clans matter less than they do in Naruto, and this section does not hide it: six marks, one row, short.
houses.greatNote: Two of the four have no name in canon. There was a fifth: the Shiba, and they fell.
houses.monNote: The crests are not canon — each is derived from the house's canonical specialty.

locations.title: Key Locations
locations.lede: The places are kept in their own worlds, and each group wears that world's skin. Scrolling down, the page changes colour five more times — this section is the page's own summary.

akatsuki.title: Akatsuki
akatsuki.subtitle: The Dawn
akatsuki.lede: Founded on a promise of peace in the shadow of the rain village; twisted into a plan to bring the world to its knees. This exhibit is the archive of that transformation.

hero.name: Pain
hero.epigraph: The world will grow the day it learns pain.

meta.eyeValue: Rinnegan — eye of the Six Paths
meta.roleValue: Face and leader of the Akatsuki

about.title: About the Akatsuki
about.p1: The Akatsuki was born on the land war burned hardest. Three orphans of Amegakure — Yahiko, Nagato, Konan — grew up in Jiraiya's shadow and built the organisation on a single promise: a world without war.
about.p2: Yahiko's death bent that promise. The search for peace became forcing peace by teaching pain; hope became a plan to collect the nine Tailed Beasts. The red-cloud cloak became the mark of blood spilled in the rain.
about.p3: Pain stands at the centre; around him, everyone who served him — and everyone who used him. The exhibit unfolds downward in that order.

goals.title: Their Goals
goals.tailsText: The chakra of the nine tailed beasts gathered into one hand; the balance of power passes from the villages to the organisation.
goals.moonText: The world cast into a single illusion; war, pain and choice ending at the same moment.
goals.peaceText: Yahiko's ideal: a world without war or pain. The first promise, left in the ashes of the plan.

about.quote: True peace is only possible when people come to understand pain.

paths.title: Six Paths of Pain
paths.lede: Six corpses, one will. Nagato's Rinnegan grants each body a path, each path a power.

deva.name: Deva Path
deva.desc: Yahiko's body; the organisation's face to the world.
deva.ability: Gravity itself — Shinra Tensei, Banshō Ten'in
deva.short: The Deva Path (天道, Tendō) grants its user the ability to direct attractive and repulsive forces on objects and people.
deva.long:
The Deva Path (天道, Tendō) grants its user the ability to direct attractive and repulsive forces on objects and people.

These techniques cannot be used in rapid succession, however; the time needed to recover after use depends on the scale of the technique performed — at least five seconds are required. Used at high intensity it not only demands a long rest, it can also shorten the user's lifespan. The Deva Path grants one further ability: Chibaku Tensei — the power to create a huge, temporary celestial body from all surrounding matter drawn to a released black sphere.

Although Nagato wielded the Deva Path's powers himself before he was crippled, he spent the rest of his life channelling this power through the body of his dead friend Yahiko, using Yahiko as the face of the Pain identity. In the anime, Nagato was shown levitating through Pain — both before flattening Konoha and during the battle against Naruto in his six-tailed form.
deva.influence: In Buddhism, the Deva realm is the realm of bliss. It is sometimes called the "realm of the gods", because its inhabitants are so powerful compared to humans that they can almost be likened to divine beings. Yet beings born into the Deva realm are still subject to rebirth. Devas wrestle with pride, and with the pain of knowing that their long lives and power will not ultimately prevent their rebirth.

asura.name: Asura Path
asura.ability: Mechanised limbs, missiles, a steel frame
asura.short: The Asura Path (修羅道, Shuradō) grants its user the ability to augment their own body, summoning mechanised armour and various ballistic and mechanical weaponry.
asura.long:
The Asura Path (修羅道, Shuradō) grants its user the ability to augment their own body, summoning mechanised armour and various ballistic and mechanical weaponry.

Throughout his life, Nagato channelled the Asura Path's power through the body of a ninja puppeteer.

Through the Asura Path the user can form four additional arms and two additional faces, and carry a folded, serrated blade-like sash around the waist. These extra limbs and the user's entire body are laced with mechanical weaponry they can access at will. The user can launch their arms as long-range projectiles, or detach them to fire clusters of segmented missiles. They can also extend flexible blades and drills from their arms, or an array of mechanical tentacles, and propel themselves forward at speed by emitting chakra blasts from vents in their feet. The user can further transform a hand into a cannon, or open the crown of their head, to release a chakra blast powerful enough to destroy many buildings at once.

The body through which Nagato channelled the Asura Path displayed raw physical strength — enough to tear off Jiraiya's arm and crush his throat with basic taijutsu, and to hurl the Animal Path from outside the village into Konohagakure. Thanks to its mechanised innards, the Asura Path could also withstand damage that would normally be fatal. All of these abilities suited the "warring demon" name the Asura Path carries, while granting it serious versatility.
asura.influence: In Buddhism, the Asura realm is the plane of semi-divine warring demons, into which one is reborn for jealousy, struggle, conflict or rationalised behaviour in a previous life; though powerful, they live in constant violence and unresolvable conflict. In keeping with a common depiction of the Asura, this ability grants the user six arms and three faces, each displaying a different emotion. Like Devas, Asuras are a race of supernatural beings. They also appear in Hinduism as divine beings known to pursue power and to live lives of hedonism and material, bodily pleasure. Both depictions are reflected in the Asura Path's abilities. It also draws on Hinduism in that mythology describes Asuras as capable of wielding magical devices resembling today's biological missiles.

human.name: Human Path
human.ability: Reads the mind it touches, tears out the soul
human.short: The Human Path (人間道, Ningendō) grants a Rinnegan user the ability to read a target's mind — down to their most hidden secrets — by placing a hand on their head or chest.
human.long:
The Human Path (人間道, Ningendō) grants a Rinnegan user the ability to read a target's mind — down to their most hidden secrets — by placing a hand on their head or chest. The process kills the target; when the user withdraws their hand, the target's soul is physically pulled from their body. This makes the ability extremely lethal at close quarters, as in most cases targets can do little to prevent the extraction of their souls — the only recourse is to attack the user, which the other Six Paths techniques make very difficult. Still, a target of sufficient strength can partially resist it physically for a time.

As part of his Six Pains, Nagato channelled the Human Path's power through the corpse of a Takigakure shinobi.

animal.name: Animal Path
animal.ability: Summoning seals — an army of giant beasts
animal.short: The Animal Path (畜生道, Chikushōdō) grants a Rinnegan user the ability to summon a variety of animals and creatures to aid them in battle.
animal.long:
The Animal Path (畜生道, Chikushōdō) grants a Rinnegan user the ability to summon a variety of animals and creatures to aid them in battle.

These creatures appear to be immortal, as they could be summoned again after being killed. Notably, summoning creatures through the Animal Path requires neither a blood sacrifice nor hand seals. The Animal Path can also summon people with hand signs, as in the case of Nagato's Paths and Konan. Tactically, the Animal Path's main role in battle appears to be overwhelming multiple opponents with a mass of summons.

In Nagato's case — channelling the Animal Path first through a Fūma clan shinobi and then, for the rest of its service, through Ajisai's corpse — the summoned creatures also appear to have chakra receivers embedded in their bodies, just like the Pain Paths. Nagato also tends to send the Animal Path into battle first, to confuse enemies about how many opponents they truly face. As these creatures display the Rinnegan as well, they serve as extensions of Nagato. During the Fourth Shinobi World War, Nagato used its summons for transport before being reanimated in a form that could move under its own power.
animal.influence: Buddhists believe that animals live in a different dimension separated from humans not spatially but mentally — called the "Tiryagyoni realm" — an unhappy plane of rebirth built on fear, instinct and survival of the strongest, suffered by animals who serve humans and are, above all, unaware of what befalls them.

preta.name: Preta Path
preta.short: The Preta Path (餓鬼道, Gakidō) grants its user the ability to absorb chakra of any kind.
preta.long:
The Preta Path (餓鬼道, Gakidō) grants its user the ability to absorb chakra of any kind. Pain channelled the Preta Path's power through the corpse of a Kusagakure shinobi.

By nature this ability is primarily defensive: it can drain a person's chakra through physical contact. Beyond that, the Preta Path can absorb and thereby neutralise pure chakra or chakra-based ninjutsu techniques. It does not absorb physical attacks such as Gaara's sand, but it can drain the sand's chakra. This is done by forming a barrier around the user's entire body, so that attacks from every direction can be absorbed.

Although this ability can also absorb senjutsu chakra, the user still runs the risk of turning into a stone statue when absorbing too much of it.

During the Fourth Shinobi World War, Nagato used the Preta Path to absorb Killer B's chakra while B was in his Version 2 form. He is then seen using that chakra to restore his body to its state before it was weakened by the Demonic Statue of the Outer Path. This also returned his hair colour from white to red and repaired the damage to his legs — though, likely due to lost muscle memory, he could not use his legs fully.

This ability can be neutralised by certain techniques capable of suppressing the opposing user's movements or chakra.
preta.influence: In Buddhism, the Preta realm (also known as the Hungry Ghost realm) is a form of rebirth rooted in strong possessiveness and desire nurtured in a previous life or lives. Pretas are humanoid creatures that are perpetually hungry and thirsty yet can never be sated, living like hopeless addicts trying to quiet an insatiable craving. In appearance, Pretas are corpse-pale, exhausted figures — unlike the bulky build of Pain's Preta Path. In Hinduism, Preta can also mean ghost, which relates to the ability the technique employs.

naraka.name: Naraka Path
naraka.ability: Before the King of Hell: interrogation and repair
naraka.short: The Naraka Path (地獄道, Jigokudō) grants its user two core abilities through the King of Hell: interrogation and restoration.
naraka.long:
The Naraka Path (地獄道, Jigokudō) grants its user two core abilities through the King of Hell: interrogation and restoration. Pain channelled the Naraka Path's power through the body of a priest.

The Naraka Path's ability rests largely on the King of Hell — a huge head that rises from the earth, wreathed in purple flames. It also possesses the Rinnegan and shares a common field of vision with the other summons.

To interrogate, the Naraka Path merely needs to seize a person, which causes the King of Hell to appear before them. While the victim is seemingly paralysed, the Naraka Path begins its questioning. Once answers are given, the King of Hell opens its mouth, releases tentacle-like arms, and draws out a manifestation of the victim's life-force energy in the shape of an enlarged tongue. The King of Hell then passes judgement. If the person lies or refuses to answer, the King of Hell tears out and eats their tongue, apparently killing them. If they tell the truth they are spared, though left utterly drained.

The Naraka Path's second ability is the restoration of any kind of damage. To do this, the Naraka Path has the King of Hell swallow the damaged body with its tentacle-like arms; after a time, the destroyed body emerges from its mouth fully renewed. It applied this, for example, to the Asura Path after it was destroyed by Chōji and Chōza Akimichi. Thanks to its restorative powers, the Naraka Path could easily be considered the most valuable body of the Six Pains when spread across six different bodies. In formation, Nagato places the Naraka Path behind the emotional Deva Path, with the other four on the front lines.

Kabuto Yakushi has stated that a Naraka Path user can transport bodies and souls using the King of Hell.
naraka.influence:
Naraka is a Sanskrit word meaning the underworld. In Hinduism it is a place where souls are sent to atone for their sins. Yama is the God of Justice and King of Hell. After death, he metes out fitting punishments to living beings — he may, for instance, plunge them into boiling oil. Lie to him and he tears out your tongue.

In Buddhism, the Naraka realm or "hell realm" is a plane of rebirth based on the Karma (deeds of body, speech and mind) accumulated in a previous life or lives. There are various Narakas, each holding beings who are tormented until their Karma reaches its full and complete result. These beings can then be reborn into a higher plane. On the uppermost level, the "Reviving" Naraka, sinners endlessly attack one another and are healed only by a cold wind — likely the inspiration for the healing power the Naraka Path wields through the King of Hell.

Naraka superficially resembles the Christian concepts of hell or purgatory, but there are many important differences between them.

members.title: Members of the Akatsuki
members.lede: Nine names under the red cloud — each one a village's loss.

itachi.role: Kisame's partner; the quietest shadow in the organisation
itachi.bio: Konoha's brightest child took its heaviest duty: erase his own clan, shoulder the guilt, live in exile. Even inside the Akatsuki his loyalty belonged to his village.
itachi.quote: Forgive me, Sasuke… there is no next time.

kisame.bio: One of Kirigakure's Seven Swordsmen. The shark-skin blade Samehada feeds on chakra; its owner never tires, his enemies run dry.
kisame.quote: It seems we are both monsters — at least I look the part.

deidara.ability: Explosive clay — from C1 to C0
deidara.bio: An artist who fled Iwagakure. To him art is a moment: it flares and is gone. His final work was himself.

sasori.ability: Puppet mastery — a hundred puppets, his own body included
sasori.bio: Sunagakure's puppet master. He sought immortality in his craft: turned his body into a puppet and kept his heart in a single capsule.
sasori.quote: True art is what endures forever.

kakuzu.bio: From Takigakure; bounty hunting keeps the organisation's ledger. Five hearts mean five separate lives — an enemy must stop every one of them.
kakuzu.quote: Everything has a price — even a life.

hidan.bio: The apostate of Yugakure. He cannot die; he counts pain as worship. Why he was paired with Kakuzu is simple: no one else could stand him.
hidan.quote: Jashin commands me to share the pain. Yours first.

konan.ability: Paper jutsu — her body unfolds into paper
konan.bio: The survivor of the three orphans. Amegakure calls her an angel; her paper wings carry even through the rain.
konan.quote: Hope is a paper flower — it blooms despite the rain.

tobi.role: Rules from the shadows with Zetsu
tobi.bio: A clowning rookie on stage; behind the mask, the organisation's true hand. He borrowed his name from the dead: Madara.

zetsu.ability: Merging with the earth · a twin body
zetsu.bio: Half white, half black; one keeps the record, the other makes the plan. Everything the Akatsuki has seen, Zetsu saw first.
zetsu.quote: We only watch… and we forget nothing.

pain.role: Leader — the face and will of the organisation
pain.bio: The single will behind six bodies. Amegakure knows him as a god; the organisation breathes by the plan born of his pain. This card is a membership record — the throne itself stands above, in the hero.
pain.quote: Feel pain. Think pain. Accept pain. Know pain.

partners.title: Partners
partners.lede: The organisation works in pairs — not out of trust, but oversight.
partners.itachi-kisame: The shadow and the monster: its quietest member and its loudest became the organisation's longest-lived pair.
partners.deidara-sasori: Two artists, two opposing schools: the explosion of the moment against the puppet of eternity.
partners.hidan-kakuzu: The zombie duo: one cannot die, the other cannot stop killing.
partners.pain-konan: From the orphanage to godhood: the two children left standing held the organisation's centre together.

history.title: History of the Akatsuki
history.lede: From a promise of peace to a world war — four eras, one end.

founding.title: Three orphans, one promise
founding.text: In the middle of a war, Amegakure's three orphans — Yahiko, Nagato, Konan — build the organisation on what Jiraiya taught them. The goal is a single sentence: peace without bloodshed.

yahiko.title: The years of hope
yahiko.text: Yahiko's charisma makes the organisation grow; the Akatsuki is a peace movement. A trap laid by Hanzō and Danzō ends the era: Yahiko dies by Nagato's hand.

nagato.title: Pain is born
nagato.text: Nagato turns Yahiko's body into the Deva Path and takes the name Pain. The red-cloud cloaks go on, the organisation splits into pairs; the target is now the nine Tailed Beasts.

war.title: The world stage
war.text: Hunting the Bijū turns every village hostile: Gaara is taken, Konoha is razed. Behind the curtain Tobi — Obito — ties the strings to Madara's design: the Fourth Great Ninja War.

end.title: Dawn breaks
end.text: Nagato listens to Naruto and, with his last strength, restores those he killed. Konan lays down the cloak; the war consumes Obito and Madara alike. One question remains: can pain teach peace?

nagato.text: If Pain is a mask, Nagato is the face: his crippled body bound to the Gedō Mazō, his will walking in six corpses.

konan.text: The only one who never questioned Nagato's decisions — until Nagato chose Naruto. That day Konan chose her own path too.

obito.text: The Tobi mask hides the hand that 'showed' Nagato his path. Pain's godhood is one act in Obito's script.

madara.text: A dead legend, a living plan: the Akatsuki's skeleton is Madara's testament; Obito merely executes it.

yahiko.text: The organisation's soul. The Deva Path is his body — every time Pain appears, a dead hope stands upright.

symbols.title: Symbolism
symbols.lede: Three marks of the organisation — each the record of a loss.

cloud.name: The Red Cloud
cloud.text: The clouds that carried war over Amegakure, and the blood spilled in that rain: the clouds on the cloak are the founders' mourning.

rings.name: The Rings
rings.text: Ten rings, ten seats. A ring does not die with its member — it is reclaimed; an empty finger is the name of a chair in the organisation.

cloak.name: The Cloak
cloak.text: Black ground, red clouds, high collar: not who you are, but what you carry. Whoever puts on the cloak leaves their name at the door.

legacy.title: Legacy
legacy.p1: When the Akatsuki ended, no fortress and no army remained; what remained was its question: can peace be built by force? Naruto's answer was born from Nagato's question.
legacy.p2: This exhibit is the record of the organisation that asked it. The red clouds settled with the rain — but they left a mark.
